item.title: The Wages of Fear | Re:Made — Tue Nov 10, 7:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
In a downtrodden South American oil town, four desperate men sign on for a suicide mission: driving trucks packed with nitroglycerin over makeshift roads and treacherous mountain terrain. The men are forced to navigate fires, bumps, and jolts, while their fortitude and friendship are put to the ultimate test: keep cool or die. The Wages of Fear is, hands down, one of the greatest thrillers of all time and a white-knuckle ride from Clouzot, France’s legendary master of suspense. [152 min; suspense, thriller; French with English subtitles]
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Wed Nov 11 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Wed Nov 11 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Wed Nov 11 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Wed Nov 11, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Going to college offers a variety of new freedoms, excitements, and difficulties as students make the transition away from home. Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Pepero Day Tabling — Wed Nov 11, 12:00 PM — 10th St and Fee at Arboretum - Table 1
item.description:
Join KSA as we celebrate Pepero Day (빼빼로데이)—one of South Korea's favorite holiday traditions! Celebrated every year on November 11th because the date 11/11 resembles four stick-shaped Pepero biscuits lined up, Pepero Day is all about sharing sweet treats and showing appreciation to friends, classmates, and loved ones. Stop by the KSA tabling station to pick up your favorite Pepero box, write cute customized gift notes, and learn more about Korean culture!
Hosted by: Korean Student Association
Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12970370

item.title: Curiosity Lab — Thu Nov 12, 4:00 PM — Wonderlab
item.description:
November Theme: Paleontology Day: Thursday Time: 4 - 5:45pm Recommended Ages: Designed for children ages 6 - 10, but siblings are welcome. Location: WonderLab Cost: Free for Members / Free with Museum Admission Curiosity Lab is an after-school, free play program for kids ages 6-10 years. Children are invited to explore, experiment, and engage in hands-on sensory activities at their own pace. No instructions, no pressure-just curiosity-driven play. Held in WonderLab \(or sometimes outdoors weather permitting\), the space is set up for exploration with a variety of rotating materials and stations. There will be one main activity/installment/manipulative for the month that will be brought out every Thursday. This will rotate with the month and the month's theme.
Source: Limestone Post

item.title: Tarot, Ancestors & Intuition: Free Workshop and Readings — Thu Nov 12, 4:00 PM — MAXWELL HALL
item.description:
Join us for an evening with artist Julie Schenkelberg for a free tarot spread workshop from 4-5 pm and free 10-minute readings from 5-7 pm at the Cook Center for Public Arts & Humanities! Learn to read a card spread using your own deck from a tarot practitioner with over 20 years of experience. Following the workshop, receive a free 10-minute reading from Julie. First come, first served for the free readings. Julie Schenkelberg was the IU Arts & Humanities Council's Engaged Artist-in-Residence in 2024 on the Bloomington campus. During her residency, she explored some of IU's collections that center spiritual mysticism at the Lilly Library, including their tarot card collection. Please RSVP to participate in the workshop. Max 12 attendance for this, waitlist available. https://www.julieschenkelberg.com/work#/new-gallery/ (https://www.julieschenkelberg.com/work#/new-gallery/)
Source: IU Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design

item.description:
November Theme: Technology Day: Friday Times 3 - 4pm Recommended for: All ages Event Price Free for Members / Free with Museum Admission Get closer to the wild side with Animal Hour and Dive Deeper! These weekly programs let you chat with WonderLab's animal experts, discover what it takes to care for creatures from around the globe, and meet snakes, lizards, insects, arachnids, and more-up close and out of their habitats. Animal Hour takes place on most Fridays, while Dive Deeper happens on the last Friday of each month at WonderLab's stunning coral reef aquarium. Type of Activities Animal Hour: Meet our animal ambassadors. Observe the tools we use to care for our animal ambassadors. Type of Activities Dive Deeper: Tour the reef system and learn the mechanics behind how it functions.

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Mon Nov 16 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Mon Nov 16 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (
